title: Fit a robot axis's side-mounted cable carrier: fold it round and click its free end into the carriage bracket
instruction: Fold the cable carrier back on itself and snap its free end into the bracket on the carriage, keeping the carriage at its mark, then let go and move both hands clear.
context: Robot linear axes, gantries and seventh-axis tracks carry their motor and encoder cables in a cable carrier (energy chain) between the bed and the moving carriage. Where the installation height is low it is mounted on its side, turned 90 degrees, as the maker recommends. Fitting it is a step of building the axis and of replacing a worn one: with its fixed end in the bed bracket, the free end is carried round in the plane of the table so the links roll into their loop, and the end link is pushed into the carriage's bracket until its upper pin clicks into the bracket's bore. The links bend only one way, to a 38 mm radius, and lock straight the other way: the hand carrying the end turns with it through 180 degrees, gripping it firmly enough to drag the chain round, while the other hand holds the lower run still so the loop forms where it should. With the motor off the carriage runs freely on its rail, so a hand braces it while the end is pushed home.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. (1) Cable carrier, igus E2 mini B15.015.038.0, black polymer, empty: 11 links of pitch 30.5 mm (335.5 mm), outer width 26 mm, outer height 23 mm, side plates 5.5 mm, bend radius 38 mm (each joint turns 0 to 47 degrees, one way only), 0.12 kg. It is mounted on its side: it lies on one side plate on the table, 26 mm tall, its inner (bending) radius facing away from the robot. Its fixed end is clipped into an igus B15 polymer bracket screwed to the table at x 27.6 to 30.7, y -0.3 to 1.9; the chain lies straight along -y between x 28 and 30.3, its free end link centred at (29.2, -32.0). The free end link ends in its pin end: over its last 16 mm both side plates are cranked in 2.75 mm, and a 6 mm pin stands on each, 6 mm from the end (the upper one flush with the chain's outer face, the lower one 1 mm short of the table). (2) Axis: an MGN12 steel rail, 360 mm, screwed to the table along y at x 47.8, from y -18 to +18. (3) Carriage: an MGN12H steel block on the rail (27 x 45 mm, its top 13 mm above the table) under a 20 mm aluminium spacer carrying a 10 mm aluminium plate (0.75 kg in all), 155 x 150 mm, from x 34.8 to 50.3 and y 0 to +15.0, its underside 3.3 cm above the table; it slides freely along the rail (motor off), +-15 cm; a yellow tape mark (15 x 6 mm) on the table beside the plate's +x edge, at y 0, lines up with the spacer's centre at the start. (4) Moving-end bracket: igus one-piece polymer mounting bracket 'with bore' for B15 (moving end of set 101-12P, black igumid G), screwed under the plate's -y end, its body at x 35.1 to 37.6 and y 0 to 1.2; its two cheeks reach back from y 0 to -1.5: one lying 0.5 mm above the table, slotted from its open end; the other 23.5 mm up, with the 6 mm bore countersunk underneath and its open end ramped underneath. Seated, the end link lies on the table between the cheeks, its pins in the slot and the bore, centred at (36.3, -1.5), turned end for end. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: Latched: the free end link sits in the bracket, its centre within 3 mm of its seat and turned within 10 degrees of it (photo with a ruler), with its upper pin clicked into the bracket's bore: the cheek lies flat on it (real trial: a 5 N pull along the chain with a luggage scale leaves it in). No tip: no link ever tipped more than 15 degrees off lying flat on its side plate (video). Carriage kept: never more than 25 mm from its tape mark (video against the mark) and within 10 mm of it at the end (ruler). Released: every fingertip 3 cm or more from every link and the bracket (video). 1.0: latched, carriage kept, released, nothing moving for 1 s (video). 0.75: latched and released but the carriage not kept, or not yet still for 1 s. 0.5: seated in the bracket and released, the pin not clicked in. 0.25: at some point the folded end link came within 3.5 cm of its seat along the rail and 4 cm overall, turned within 15 degrees of it (video). A link tipped at any time scores 0; otherwise 0.
reset_notes: Lift the bracket's upper cheek with a thumbnail and slide the end link out; lay the chain straight along -y on its side on its tape line; slide the carriage back to its tape mark.
fidelity: Links are rigid bodies on vertical pin joints with stops at straight and 47 degrees (bend radius 38 mm), no play; the chain stays flat on the table (the tip rule is for real trials) and its links do not collide with each other. The bracket's upper cheek flexes on a spring: the click takes about 5 N along the chain; igus gives no figure, so check the real one with a force gauge. Its lower cheek is slotted here. The carriage is a slide joint.
